subject: Maths
title: Simplifying algebraic fractions
subtitle: Fractions — Secondary · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can simplify algebraic fractions by factorising and cancelling common factors.

key_vocab.definition: To simplify an algebraic fraction, factorise the numerator and denominator, then cancel common factors.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can simplify algebraic fractions by factorising and cancelling common factors.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: simplify -- To simplify an algebraic fraction, factorise the numerator and denominator, then cancel common factors.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Factorise numerator and denominator completely, then cancel any factors that appear in both.
&frac{x² − 4}{x + 2} = &frac{(x+2)(x−2)}{x+2} = x − 2
Cancel the common factor (x + 2)

Key examples:
  ✓ &frac{4x}{8} = &frac{x}{2}  (divide by 4)
  ✓ &frac{x²+x}{x} = x + 1  (factorise and cancel x)
  ✓ &frac{x²−4}{x+2} = x − 2  (difference of two squares)
  ✗ &frac{x+3}{x+5} = &frac{3}{5}  (cannot cancel x from a sum)
  ✗ &frac{x²+1}{x} = x + 1  (x²+1 does not factorise over x)

sections.title: Worked Example
Mixed simplification
Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ &frac{x² − 4}{x + 2} = x − 2
✗ &frac{x + 3}{x + 5} = &frac{3}{5}
✓ &frac{x² + 3x}{x} = x + 3
✗ &frac{x² + 4}{x + 2} = x + 2
✓ You must factorise before cancelling

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Common numerical factors:
  (a) &frac{2x}{3}
  (b) 3x
  (c) 5x
  (d) 3x

Factorising the numerator:
  (a) x + 2
  (b) x + 2
  (c) x − 5
  (d) x + 2

Difference of two squares:
  (a) x − 2
  (b) x + 4
  (c) x − 5
  (d) x − 1

Quadratic numerator:
  (a) x + 3
  (b) x + 4
  (c) x − 3
  (d) x + 4

Mixed simplification:
  (a) 5
  (b) &frac{x − 3}{x + 3}
  (c) x − 2
  (d) &frac{x − 3}{x − 4}
  (e) &frac{x − 3}{x + 3}
